evidence.reason: The blackout gate is existing intended behavior with explicit semantics in the same file: blackout() docstring 'GLM peak hours: no repair dispatch at all' and blocked() 'No dispatch inside the blackout, nor one whose wall clock would reach it.' The current code shows the triage path reaching a judge dispatch with no blackout check anywhere near it: drain() validates worker_limit and checks dispatch_paused() (the provider rate-limit cooldown, a different gate), then calls fetch_clone() (line 624) which can block up to TICK_LOCK_WAIT_S=300 s on the tick lock, then runs triage_phase() (line 629), whose judge() closure calls dispatch() directly at lines 593-594. No blocked()/blackout() call appears in drain() before triage or inside triage_phase()/judge(); the only gate rechecked after the wait is dispatch_paused() (provider cooldowns), confirming the code's own pattern of rechecking gates after time-consuming phases while omitting the blackout gate for these judge dispatches. So a blackout that begins during the tick-lock wait or during the triage pass admits judge model calls, violating blocked()'s stated invariant (the wall-clock reach margin computed at the earlier check is consumed by the wait). This is an implementation gap in an existing enforcement mechanism, not a proposal to enlarge scope: the recommendation to recheck blocked() before each dispatch merely enforces the documented 'no repair dispatch at all' window. The finding's cited line numbers are stale (main at 826, dispatch at 567/753 from an older blob), but the defect is verifiable at the current dispatch site; the recovery-path details could not be independently confirmed due to truncation, but the triage-path evidence alone sustains the finding.
